Usual and average: your usual is the median of your recent days and your average is the mean. The usual resists one odd night; the average follows it. Apex shows both and places today against your usual.
HRV stability is how much your overnight HRV varied over 7 nights. The normal range is half a standard deviation around your baseline; the weekly HRV can sit within, above or below it.
Shortfall vs 7 h adds up the nights shorter than 7 hours in the last week. It is a secondary view next to your personal sleep debt, not a debt you owe.

Sleep midpoint is halfway through the night; midpoint variability is how much it moved over 7 nights. WASO is time awake after falling asleep, awakenings per hour counts wake events longer than 3 minutes, and the Sleep Regularity Index is how repeatable your sleep and wake times are.

Sedentary time, prolonged sitting bouts, the longest bout, breaks per hour and peak 30-minute cadence are counted from minute-by-minute steps for a finished day. When the steps are missing or too coarse, Apex says so instead of guessing.
A pattern card appears only when several signals moved away from your usual together. It uses cautious wording, is not a diagnosis, and stays quiet when data quality is low.
